translations.text: James, servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes scattered abroad: greetings (literally, rejoice)!
Count it all joy, my brothers, whenever you fall into trials of various kinds;
know that this testing of your faith produces patience,
and let patience have its complete work, so that you may be complete and wholly alive, lacking in nothing.
If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask it of God, who gives to all freely and reproaches no one, and he will give it to him.
But let him ask in faith and without doubting, for whoever doubts is like the waves of the sea, stirred up and tossed about by the wind.
Let that man not suppose that he will receive anything from the Lord.
A double-minded man is unstable in all his ways.
Let the lowly brother boast in his exaltation,
and the rich man in his humiliation, for like the flower of the grass, so will he pass away.
The sun rose with its heat and withered the grass, and its flower fell, and the beauty of its appearance perished. So also the rich man will wither away in his going.
Blessed is the man who endures trial, for when he has been proved he will receive the crown of life, which God promised to those who love him.
Let no one who is tempted say, "I am tempted by God," for God cannot be tempted by evil, and he tempts no one.
But each person is tempted by his own desire, being drawn away and compelled.
Then that desire conceives and gives birth to sin, and that sin becomes full-grown and gives birth to death for him.
Do not be deceived, my beloved brothers!
Every good thing given and every perfect gift comes down from above, from the Father of light, with whom there is no change or shift of a turning shadow.
By his own will he gave birth to us by the word of truth, so that we might be a kind of first beginning of his creatures.
So know this now, my beloved brothers: let every man be quick to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger.
For the anger of man does not do the righteousness of God.
Therefore let all filthiness and the excess of wickedness be removed from you; with meekness receive the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.
And be doers of this word, and not hearers only, bringing contempt upon yourselves.
If anyone is only a hearer of this word and not a doer, such a person is like the man who looks at his own appearance in a mirror;
and as soon as he goes away, he immediately forgets what he is like.
But whoever has looked into the perfect law of freedom and has stayed with it, and has become not a forgetful hearer but a doer of the work, that person will be blessed in his doing.
If [?] the service of God, and does not bridle his own tongue, he deceives himself, and his service is vain.
But pure and undefiled service before God and the Father is this: to look after orphans and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained by this world.
My brothers, do not hold the faith of our glorious Lord Jesus Christ with partiality.
If a man comes into your assembly wearing a gold ring and dressed in bright clothing, and a poor man also comes in, in filthy clothing,
and you look to the one who is dressed in the bright clothing and say to him, "You sit here in a good place," but to the poor man you say, "You stand," or "Sit beneath my feet,"
you have become divided in heart, and have become judges with evil thoughts of the heart.
Listen, my beloved brothers: has not God chosen the poor of the world, but rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom, which God promised to those who love him?
But you have dishonored the poor man. Is it not the rich who oppress you, and are they not the very ones who drag you before the judge?
Are they not the very ones who blaspheme the good name that is called upon you?
If you fulfill the royal law, as it is written, "You shall love your neighbor as yourself," you do well.
If you show partiality, you sin, and the law convicts you as transgressors.
For whoever fulfills the whole law and stumbles in one point has become guilty of all of it.
For he who said, "Do not commit adultery," also said, "Do not kill." If you do not commit adultery and do not kill, but do not have love, you have still become a transgressor of the law.
So speak and so act as those who are to be judged by the law of freedom.
For judgment is merciless toward those who have not shown mercy; [?] boast of mercy over judgment.
What profit is there, my brothers, if someone says, "I have faith," but has no works? That faith alone cannot give him life.
If a brother or a sister is naked and lacking daily food,
and one of you says to them, "Go in peace, be filled and be warmed," but you do not give them what the body needs, what profit is there?
So also faith: if it has no works, it is dead by itself.
If someone says, "You have faith and I have works": show me your faith without your works, and I will show you faith by my works.
You believe that God is one; you know that well. The demons also believe it and tremble before him, but they do not do his will.
Do you want to know, O worthless man, that faith without works is dead?
Was not Abraham our father justified by works, when he offered up Isaac his son on the altar?
Do you see that faith helped his works, and by those works that faith was made complete?
And the scripture was fulfilled which says, "Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness," and he was called the friend of God.
Do you see that a person is justified by works, and not by faith alone?
In the same way, was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she received the messengers in peace and sent them out by another way?
Just as the body without the spirit is dead, so also faith without works is dead.
Do not many of you become teachers, my brothers! Know that we will receive a greater judgment.
For we all err greatly. But whoever does not err in speech is a perfect man; he is able to bridle his whole body as well.
If we put bridles on a horse to make it obey us, we turn it and its whole body.
And look, even the very great ships, driven about by fierce winds, are turned by a small rudder wherever the steersman wishes to go.
In the same way, the tongue is a small member, yet it boasts greatly. Look again: how much material a small fire sets ablaze!

And the tongue too is a fire, an adornment of falsehood. The tongue is set among our members; it defiles the whole body and sets on fire the wheel of creation, and it is itself set on fire by Gehenna.
Every kind of beast and bird, of creeping thing and swimming creature, is tamed and has been tamed by humankind.
But no one is able to tame the human tongue. It is an evil that cannot be restrained, full of deadly poison.
For with it we bless God and the Father, and with it we curse people, who were created in the likeness of God.
From the same mouth come blessing and cursing. My beloved brothers, it is not right for this to be so.
Does sweet and bitter water flow from the same opening of a spring?
My brothers, can a fig tree bear olives, or a vine figs? In the same way, salt [?] water cannot become sweet.
Who among you is wise and knowledgeable? Let him show his good [?] works with the meekness of wisdom.
Where do the fights and quarrels among you come from? Either [?] or [?] from desires.
You desire and do not have; you kill and are envious, and cannot obtain; you quarrel and fight, and you have nothing, because you do not ask.
You ask and do not receive, because you ask wickedly.
Or do you think that the Scripture says in vain: "The spirit that dwells in us longs to the point of envy"?
Rather, it is for the giving of grace. That is why it says: "He crushes the proud, but gives grace to the humble."
Submit to God, resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double-minded.
Humble yourselves, mourn and weep. Let your laughter be turned to mourning and your joy to sorrow.
Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will lift you up.
